newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan lifts all controls on foreign transfers.
newsitem.headline: Jordan lifts all controls on foreign transfers.

text.p: Jordan's Central Bank on Sunday announced it had lifted all foreign exchange controls to boost foreign investments and enhance confidence in the local currency.
Jordan Central Bank Governor, Ziyad Fariz, said the move taken by the bank's board was a further step towards liberalisation of the financial sector.
He said it did away with all foreign exchange restrictions on capital transfers by Jordanians and corporate entities.
"There are no longer any foreign exchange controls whatsoever, (there is) free movement of capital," Fariz told Reuters.
The new rules end restrictions on Jordanians transfering funds for personal needs and for the first time allows free movement of capital by Jordanians for investment purposes.
Prior to the move Jordanians investing capital abroad had to seek approval on a case by case basis.
Limits had been imposed after a sharp devaluation of the dinar in 1989, sparked by an economic crisis.

Bankers say the Central Bank was encouraged in the timing of the move after net foreign currency cash reserves reached $1 billion, or close to the 1997 target, after record inflows of capital in the first half of the year.
Jordan has over the last two years liberalised foreign exchange controls and allowed banks to invest its foreign currency deposits in international capital markets.
